callout.text: Just a kid trying to survive.

storyboard.claim: Buck started as a small-time hustler, just a kid trying to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck on a city street corner — young, wary, doing what he had to do.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues Buck's backstory introduced at the end of chunk 2.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Buck's origin as ordinary — a kid, not a criminal by nature.

storyboard.claim: After Pop died, something in Buck shifted — 'there's that nighttime.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck slumped in shadow — the grief of a lost father figure pulling him down.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The before to the after: Buck was ordinary, then Pop died.
storyboard.addedInformation: The 'nighttime' is the mother's phrase — an inherited warning, now landed.

callout.text: put a gun in his hand

storyboard.claim: The nighttime put a gun in Buck's hand and made him predatory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gun icon beside Buck, angry and hardened — the transformation is complete.
storyboard.onScreenText: put a gun in his hand
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism of the shift: grief → the nighttime → the gun.
storyboard.addedInformation: 'Sharp in his teeth' is the narrator's phrase — the literal gun makes it concrete.

storyboard.claim: The environment feralizes you — strips your humanity and forces you to play apex predator just to survive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck on the street, angry and talking — the environment itself is the force shaping him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Hosts interpret Buck's transformation as environmental pressure, not character flaw.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the 'apex predator' metaphor cannot be drawn; the angry street man is the closest visual claim.

storyboard.claim: One host read Buck's question as a challenge — pushing Will to prove he has the guts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck pointing at Will with a smirk — reading as a dare or test of manhood.
storyboard.onScreenText: What you need a gun for
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first host's interpretation of Buck's role in the elevator.
storyboard.addedInformation: Buck's smirk frames the question as a dare; Will is small and afraid beside him.

storyboard.claim: The reading: Buck is pushing Will to step up, to claim the violent inheritance passed down to him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Inheritance icon — the gun as a legacy being handed from Buck to Will.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the 'test' reading: it's about lineage and manhood.
storyboard.addedInformation: The inheritance icon reads as estate/legacy — exactly what the gun represents here.

storyboard.claim: But look closer — Buck's body language tells a different story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close-up on Buck's blank, tired face — not a dare, something else.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second host pivots: the 'test' reading is wrong.
storyboard.addedInformation: Close-up on the face forces the viewer to read the expression, not the posture.

storyboard.claim: Buck scoffs, shakes his head — it isn't encouragement. It's mockery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck with a dismissive smirk, talking — reads as contempt, not support.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reframes the previous beats: same gesture, opposite meaning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Smirk carries the edge of someone who knows the answer is absurd.

storyboard.claim: Buck knows firsthand the gun doesn't work — he's standing there with a bullet hole front and back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The gun icon, Buck slumped and sad — the weapon that killed him is the same weapon Will holds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The physical proof of the mockery: Buck is dead because of the rules.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gun icon next to a slumped Buck makes the failure of the gun literal.

storyboard.claim: The gun didn't save Buck. The rules didn't save him. He's looking at a terrified 15-year-old holding the same weapon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck pointing at Will — the rules icon struck through: they failed him, they will fail Will too.
storyboard.onScreenText: The rules did not save him
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From mockery to the concrete evidence: the rules are a lie, proven by Buck's death.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike style signals the rules are being rejected by the narration.

storyboard.claim: Will holds the weapon that failed Buck, realizing the absolute absurdity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone with the gun icon — afraid, thinking, the absurdity landing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Buck's point lands on Will — now Will registers it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gun icon anchors 'the weapon that failed him' without needing to show Buck again.

storyboard.claim: The original architect of the rules is the one pointing out they're broken.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Buck pointing — sad, not triumphant — the man who built the foundation exposing it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names Buck's role: not a mentor, but a broken architect.
storyboard.addedInformation: Buck's sad face prevents this reading as pride; it reads as regret.

storyboard.claim: Buck shows the futility of the rules. The next ghost will destroy the logic entirely.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rules icon struck — Buck talking, blank and hollow, as the next ghost is announced.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Buck's testimony closes; the setup for the next ghost opens.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike on the rules icon signals escalation — the logic itself will be demolished.

storyboard.claim: Floor six: the elevator doors open and a girl gets in. Will doesn't recognize her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor counter icon showing six; Dani walks in — small, lavender dress, quiet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new floor, a new ghost — the elevator's structure as the poem's clock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Walk action reads as entering — Dani arriving in the elevator before Will places her.

storyboard.claim: She grew up gorgeous in the afterlife — a heartbreaking detail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani standing quietly — the girl she never got to be, calm and present.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Will can't place her yet — she is older than he remembers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Neutral expression on a ghost child is quietly devastating; no need to signal grief explicitly here.

storyboard.claim: She speaks and he recognizes her — the girl whose life was stolen before she even knew the rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani and Will facing each other — she is sad, small, a ghost; he recognizes her now.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recognition: the girl Will knew is here, dead, and younger than the rules.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two-shot establishes the relationship — Will's grief at placing her is the beat's claim.

storyboard.claim: Kids in the park. A drive-by. She was hit. Dead before she ever learned the rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani falling — afraid — on the street; the stray bullet, the park, the innocence of it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The backstory of how she died — the most innocent casualty of the cycle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Falling + afraid reads as shot/falling — the closest the rig can get to a child struck by a bullet.

storyboard.claim: Dani's presence is devastating — she is the most important witness against rule number three: revenge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani standing quietly beside the rules icon — a child testifying against the system that killed her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names her function: not just a ghost — a structural argument against revenge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rules icon lets the muted viewer connect her presence to the specific rule being challenged.

storyboard.claim: Revenge operates on strict transactional math — a system of debt and repayment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram: kill → repayment → balance — the cold logic of revenge made explicit.
storyboard.onScreenText: Kill my brother → I kill you → Ledger balanced.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the system Dani's presence will destroy — sets up the contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: Flow diagram here is the structural beat: the logic of revenge as a closed equation.

storyboard.claim: You kill my brother, I kill you. The ledger is balanced. An eye for an eye.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The balance icon — two sides weighed equally — the logic of retributive justice stated plainly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the same flow as beat 98 in the narrator's concrete words.
storyboard.addedInformation: Balance reads as weighing/fairness — which is exactly how revenge is rationalized.

storyboard.claim: Dani asks 'What you need a gun for?' — and it strips away Will's entire tough-guy facade.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani talking to Will — small and calm, asking the impossible question; Will's mask crumbles.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dani is now the active agent — her question is the weapon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dani as the speaker (first cast, expression neutral/knowing) with Will reactive beside her.

storyboard.claim: How do you explain the math of revenge to an 8-year-old girl who was just collateral damage?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will trying to explain, surprised — Dani watching him; the gap between the logic and the child.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question is posed to Will directly — he has to answer it, and can't.
storyboard.addedInformation: Surprised reads as 'wow/realization' — Will caught without an answer.

storyboard.claim: You can't explain it. Vengeance makes zero sense to the innocent. Will tries to hold it together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone, worried and thinking — the logic has collapsed inside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer arrives: he can't explain it. The argument is over.
storyboard.addedInformation: Will thinking + worried reads as internal collapse, not external confrontation.

storyboard.claim: He realizes he has peed himself. His brain wants to be an assassin; his body reacts like a frightened child.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped and afraid — the body has given up the pretense the mind was maintaining.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The collapse becomes physical — the body makes the argument the mind refused to.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump + afraid is the closest the rig gets to the physical humiliation without depicting it explicitly.

storyboard.claim: A frightened child — the ultimate humiliation. One host reads Dani's role as making Will feel guilt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped, afraid, beside Dani — the 15-year-old reduced to childhood by a 10-year-old ghost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the body has revealed: he is a child, not a soldier.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dani's presence anchors the comparison — one ghost-child exposing one terrified living child.

storyboard.claim: Guilt is a sophisticated emotion — it requires a stable moral framework. Dani is there to trigger it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will thinking alone in abstract space — the interior argument about guilt being named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first host's theory: Dani = guilt trigger. The second host is about to disagree.
storyboard.addedInformation: Abstract set signals this is the hosts reasoning, not the story moment.

storyboard.claim: The second host disagrees: it isn't guilt he's feeling when the warm liquid runs down his leg.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped and afraid — the physical fact, not a moral one. Strike on 'not guilt.'
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot: the first host said guilt; the second host says no.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike style signals the explicit rejection of the previous frame.

storyboard.claim: It is profound, shattering embarrassment — not guilt. Think about what the rules require.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rules icon beside Will thinking — embarrassment is an attack on the rules' demands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the correct emotion and pivots to its mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rules icon connects the embarrassment to its source: the code that forbids weakness.

storyboard.claim: The rules demand a mask of unbreakable, unfeeling manhood. Don't cry. Be stoic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The mask icon; Will blank and still — performing the requirement of the rules.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the rules demand — and what Will has just failed to maintain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mask reads as 'false public face, pretending' — the literal function of the rules' code.

storyboard.claim: Be violent, be a soldier. But Dani reduces Will to what he actually is: a scared, wet kid.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped and afraid beside small, calm Dani — the gap between the role and the reality.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mask is gone — what's beneath it is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: The contrast of Dani's calm and Will's collapse makes the reduction visible.

storyboard.claim: The embarrassment shatters the armor of the rules — because the rules cannot tolerate vulnerability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rules icon; Will slumped and afraid — the code and the boy who just broke it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names why embarrassment is so lethal to the system: it proves the armor was always fake.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'shattering armor' is a metaphor — the icon + slumped body is the best literal rendering.

storyboard.claim: It exposes the cosplay — he's playing dress-up in dead Shawn's clothes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The mask icon; Will blank and still — the costume exposed, the performance over.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The 'cosplay' metaphor: Will was wearing his brother's identity, not his own.
storyboard.addedInformation: Mask is the right icon — the narration literally says it's a performance, a costume.

storyboard.claim: He wants to be a cold-blooded killer but his body won't let him lie to himself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone, afraid and thinking — the body's veto against the mind's performance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to Will's internal split before posing the next analytical question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Think + afraid reads as internal reckoning — the body arguing with the decision.

storyboard.claim: Wouldn't moral horror be enough to stop him? Not for a teenager in this environment. Guilt is abstract.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will thinking in abstract space — the hosts reasoning about why guilt doesn't work here.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The hosts pursue the embarrassment-vs-guilt question analytically.
storyboard.addedInformation: Abstract set signals conceptual argument rather than narrative scene.

storyboard.claim: Guilt can be rationalized away: 'He killed my brother. He deserves it.'
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will angry and talking — the rationalization he has available, spoken aloud.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the specific script Will uses to neutralize guilt.
storyboard.addedInformation: Angry + talk reads as someone making their case — exactly the rationalizing voice.

storyboard.claim: Embarrassment is an attack on identity. He pees himself — the illusion of competence is destroyed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will slumped and afraid — the identity he built has collapsed in a single physical moment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrast with the previous beat: guilt can be argued away; embarrassment cannot.
storyboard.addedInformation: Slump + afraid is the body's final verdict — the identity argument is over.

storyboard.claim: Dani forces the question: how do the rules account for a dead child?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dani talking beside the rules icon — the question she poses that the rules cannot answer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pulls back to Dani's structural function — she is the question the system can't handle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dani's neutral/knowing expression is her signature — she doesn't need to be angry to be devastating.

storyboard.claim: The rules have no vocabulary for her — which leaves Will entirely undefended when his father arrives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Will alone, afraid and still — the gap where the rules used to be, now exposed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rules fail completely; the transition to the next ghost begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Will's stillness and fear signal he has no script left — the armor is gone before Pop arrives.

storyboard.claim: Floor five. Pop — Will's grandfather figure — steps into the elevator.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The floor counter icon at five; Pop walking in — older, worn, sorrowful even before he speaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The elevator's structure continues — a new floor, a new and heavier ghost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Walk reads as entering the elevator; worried face signals what he carries before anyone asks.

storyboard.claim: Worry washes over Pop's face when Uncle Mark asks Will if he knows the true story of his father's death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Close-up on Pop's worried face; Mark is there — Pop's expression says everything before a word is spoken.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The detail that caught the host's attention — Pop's face as testimony.
storyboard.addedInformation: Close-up is essential here: the beat is entirely about a face reading as revelation.
